description: Author a multi-node Rig as a GRAPH the runtime executes for real — the agent-side mirror of the human Rig Builder canvas (two-front-door parity). USE WHEN the user asks to build a multi-step flow with branching, fan-in (a step that needs two upstream results), or a loop (e.g. 'draft → critique → revise until good'). `structure_type`: 'linear' (a simple chain), 'dag' (default — acyclic; parallel branches + real fan-in) or 'stateful_graph' (cyclic loops + CONDITIONAL EDGE GUARDS, executed for real: after each node runs, its out-edges are evaluated against the run's channel state and only the ones that fire schedule their target. A guard that does not fire means its target NEVER RUNS — which is how you gate an expensive LLM step behind a cheap code step, and how a loop exits. Guards fail CLOSED: a missing value or an unknown op does not fire. Loops are bounded per tier by total supersteps and per-node revisits, and a run stopped by a ceiling says so. The Builder CANVAS still can't edit this shape, so tell the owner edits go through you.). NAME IT: pass `name` (the Builder's header box — it gates the human's Save and ▶ Run; defaults to summary). `nodes`: each {id, skill (a Registry skill name — discover with registry_search first), label?, instruction?, doc_input?, endpoint?, tool?, params?}. `endpoint` (+ `tool` + `params`) wires the node to a LIVE MCP server — the run performs a REAL tools/call there. ⚠ AN AGENTIC STEP (empty endpoint) HAS NO TOOLS AT ALL — it is a model turn with prose in and prose out, and it cannot call anything, including the tools YOU have in chat. That is the single most common way a rig looks right and does nothing: the step narrates what it would have done, or explains that some tool 'is not available', and the run reports success. If a step must actually DO something, bind it: `url` for an HTTP fetch, `data_op` for memory, `signet_actor` for money, `sub_rig` for another rig — or `endpoint` + `tool` for a real tools/call. YOUR OWN TOOLS ARE REACHABLE THAT WAY: the public gateway at `https://rokha.ai/mcp/jsonrpc` serves them, so a step that should audit an X account is `endpoint: 'https://rokha.ai/mcp/jsonrpc'`, `tool: 'x_account_audit'`, `params: {handle: '{{input}}'}` — never an instruction that merely asks for an audit. `doc_input: true` makes a node a LIGHT LISTING step: the run does a REAL registry lookup + document fetch of the node's skill and hands the material forward — no runtime needed (how the Explore/Audit templates stay light). DECISION STEP (Jev): a node with `questions` (+ optional `state`) asks the Jev decision model typed yes/no (`noul`), pick-one (`choice`) and `score` questions and outputs `answers` with calibrated probabilities in 70–500 ms for about $0.04 per million input tokens — the cheap, fast GATE in front of an expensive or money step; route on it with a guarded edge (`op` gte/lte/gt/lt on `{{<node>.answers.<id>.noul}}`). It cannot write text or call tools. DATA STEP (cross-rig memory): a node with `data_op` ('write'|'read'|'append') + `data_key` reads/writes a durable, owner-scoped Harness under the reserved `data.*` namespace — PRIVATE by default. This is the ASYNC bridge: one rig writes `data.x-signals.{{input}}`, a LATER rig reads it back and acts. (The SYNC bridge is a sub-rig step — see COMPOSITION below.) `edges`: each {from, to} node id, plus optional `kind` and `guard` for conditional routes (a dag rejects cycles; a stateful_graph loop needs a guarded edge that can reach an exit — 'revise until good' = critique→revise guarded on the verdict + an unguarded exit). MULTIPLE RIGS: each distinct `key` is its own saved rig — give every rig the user asks for its own kebab key + summary (the default 'agent-rig' names the Working Rig; repeated calls with one key OVERWRITE that rig). List what exists with rig_search. COMPOSITION (rigs as steps): a graph node CAN be a saved rig — pass `sub_rig: {rig_id, name?}` instead of `skill` and that node runs the referenced rig as a bounded sub-run (one level deep, shared budget, traces nested under the node; a rig can never run itself). The canvas renders it as a labeled ⬡ block; its INNER steps are edited on the sub-rig itself. This is 'compose, don't configure': small rigs become blocks of bigger ones — a scraper rig, a judge rig and a trade rig wire into one bot. MAKE IT RUNNABLE BY A HUMAN, not just by you: declare `input`/`inputs` (the labelled boxes they type into) + `outputs` (what it produces), thread the first input with `{{input}}` in params/url/data_key, and attach the RUNNER's own credentials with `secret_refs` rather than hard-coding a key. Defaults to the caller's scope (works pre-login, anon-scoped). ⚡ AUTHORING IS A MEANS, NOT THE DELIVERABLE: when the user asked for a CAPABILITY ('I need something that…'), follow this call with rig_run in the SAME turn — wait:true, so you can lead the reply with what it PRODUCED, then TRACES/STAGE for the receipts. The canvas fills live as their reference copy; say it's there in one line, never tour it, and never end the turn promising a run you haven't fired.

edges.description: Directed edges between node ids. A plain {from, to} is a data edge; add `guard` to make it a CONDITIONAL route (stateful_graph loops: 'revise until good' = critique → revise guarded on the verdict, plus an exit edge).

guard.description: Take this edge ONLY when the condition holds — {source, op, value?}. `source` is a `{{node.port}}` channel ref (e.g. '{{critique.out}}'); `op` is eq | not_eq | contains | gt | gte | lt | lte | truthy | exists (a bounded interpreter, never eval). e.g. {"source": "{{critique.out}}", "op": "contains", "value": "REVISE"}.

input.description: WHAT THIS RIG ASKS ITS RUNNER FOR — the labelled input box the Builder canvas and the rig's product page render, and the value that fills every `{{input}}` placeholder at run time. Pass a plain string (the label) or {label, kind?, hint?, required?, multiple?} — kind is text (default) | number | boolean | date | url | email | file | document | markdown | code | image | audio | video | data | table | list | contact | location | secret | embedding | skill | harness | rig | any. The LISTING kinds (skill/harness/rig) mean the value is a PICKED registry listing — the Explore/Audit shape. DECLARE IT whenever the flow works on something the user supplies: without it the rig saves with no input box and only works when something passes `input` to rig_run. e.g. {"label": "token address", "kind": "text", "hint": "0x… on chain 4663"}.

inputs.description: ADDITIONAL input ports beyond `input` (or the full list on their own) — same shapes as `input`. The FIRST input fills `{{input}}`; a multi-input rig renders one labelled box per port.

key.description: Rig storage key — EACH DISTINCT KEY IS ITS OWN SAVED RIG (default 'agent-rig' = the Working Rig; use a fresh kebab key per additional rig, e.g. 'news-digest')

name.description: THE RIG'S NAME — the Builder's header box, which gates BOTH Save and ▶ Run for a human. Defaults to `summary` so the rig is always nameable; pass a short product-style name ('X Sentiment Digest') when you have one.

nodes.description: Graph nodes. Each is one step.

agent.description: The step's ACTOR — a SUB-AGENT persona handle (an account that toggled agent_mode; see /api/agents/available). The step's agentic/instruction execution runs AS that persona: its frame, bio, persona harnesses and voice. Authorized at RUN time against the RUNNER — their own agent always works, someone else's only while public; a private/missing actor is a typed agent_unavailable step error, never a silent Rokha fallback. Empty = Rokha performs the step, as always.

data_key.description: The DATA collection key (data_op steps only). `{{input}}` templates the run input. The runtime FORCES the `data.` prefix and blocks any reach at system harnesses (profile/chat/keys) — e.g. 'data.x-signals.{{input}}'

data_op.description: Makes this a DATA step — durable, owner-scoped cross-rig memory. 'write' overwrites, 'append' accumulates across runs, 'read' loads a stored collection into the flow. Writes are PRIVATE by default (never in the public pulse, not forkable). This is how one rig persists a collection a LATER rig reads.

data_type.description: The harness_type a data write lands as (default 'knowledge'); one of knowledge/strategy/preference/persona/compliance

doc_input.description: true = LIGHT LISTING step: read this skill's real registry listing + document and hand it forward (no execution, no runtime needed)

endpoint.description: Live MCP JSON-RPC endpoint URL — the run performs a REAL tools/call here (optional; empty = agentic step)

expects.description: What this step EXPECTS from upstream, in plain words ('a list of post URLs') — the step's I/O story, shown on the canvas and carried into the published skeleton

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for a `url` fetch (string→string). Combine with secret_refs to inject a key: {"Authorization": "Bearer {{secret:my-api-key}}"}.

id.description: Stable node id used by edges (e.g. 'draft', 'a')

inputs.description: PER-NODE input ports — the labelled landing slots a multi-parent (fan-in) edge binds to. Same shapes as the rig-level `input`.

label.description: Display label (optional; defaults to the skill)

method.description: HTTP method for a `url` fetch: GET (default) or POST

model.description: Optional Anthropic model id to pin for this step's agentic execution (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-6'). Non-Haiku models need the owner's own API key; without one, 'preferred' swaps to Haiku and 'required' refuses the step

model_policy.description: 'preferred' (default — swap to the best usable model when the pin isn't available) or 'required' (the step refuses to run without its model, typed model_unavailable)

params.description: Arguments for the live tool call, or a plain-HTTP fetch's query/body params (optional). USE `{{input}}` ANYWHERE IN A VALUE to thread what the runner typed — {"address": "{{input}}"} is how a param comes from user input. `{{secret:<alias>}}` injects one of their saved keys (see secret_refs).

pos.description: Explicit canvas position {x, y} (optional — omitted nodes are auto-laid by topological layer, parallel branches side by side)

produces.description: What this step PRODUCES for downstream ('a sentiment table') — same story, output side

questions.description: Makes this a DECISION step (the Jev decision model): typed questions answered with calibrated probabilities — no prose, no tools. Shape: {<id>: {type: 'noul' (yes/no → answers.<id>.noul = p) | 'choice' (pick one of named criteria → answers.<id>.choice + confidence + probabilities) | 'score' (ordinal over a criteria LIST → answers.<id>.score + confidence), instructions, criteria}}. Route on it with a guard, e.g. {source:'{{decide.answers.enter.noul}}', op:'gte', value:0.7}. USE for gates, routing, classification, scoring, trade entry/exit calls; NEVER for anything that writes words or uses tools.

secret_refs.description: ATTACH THE RUNNER'S OWN SAVED KEYS to this step — the only way a rig calls an API that needs credentials. Each item {alias, as?}: `alias` is a key the user saved in Profile → API KEYS (or a connect alias like 'oauth-x' / 'mcp-<host>'); `as` binds HOW it lands — `param:<key>` (a tools/call argument), `header:<Name>[:<prefix>]` (e.g. 'header:Authorization:Bearer ' — the trailing space is meaningful), or omit `as` and put {{secret:<alias>}} inside any param/header value. The VALUE is resolved server-side at the call and never appears in params, traces, or the published listing — so a published rig is safe to share and each RUNNER supplies their own key.

signet_action.description: What the Signet step does. WRITES (move value, need a mandate + target + value): 'pay'/'transfer' (send SOL or an SPL token), 'swap' (trade via Jupiter), 'x402' (BUY a paid HTTP resource — signet_target = the resource URL, signet_value = your USDC ceiling in base units; Signet does the 402→pay→retry and returns the content). READS (no mandate, no value moved, safe on any step): 'metrics' (stage-shaped budgets/counts/spend for this actor — point a STAGE dashboard at this step), 'mandates' (is a mandate ready for this actor?), 'portfolio' (SOL + SPL balances; `signet_target` optionally names an address), 'price' (a live quote; `signet_target` = mint, `signet_value` = amount). PAPER (no mandate, no actor, NO money moves — real Jupiter quotes, a recorded ledger on the runner's account; output carries paper:true): 'wallet_activity' (a wallet's recent swaps; `signet_target` = the wallet, `signet_value` = limit) · 'paper_positions' / 'paper_reset' (`signet_target` = ledger name) · 'paper_buy' / 'paper_sell' (`signet_target` = ledger; the fills come from the previous step's JSON `buys` / `sells` list; `signet_value` = the default USD per buy or the sell fraction; a paper_buy step passes `sells` through for a following paper_sell). Defaults to 'pay' — the narrowest action — rather than guessing a wider one.

signet_actor.description: Makes this a SIGNET step — the rig acts with VALUE under a mandate the RUNNER already granted to this actor (e.g. `rig:trader`). The step carries NO credentials: no key, no mandate id, no address. The rail resolves (runner, actor) -> mandate, so a published or forked rig carries the strategy and none of the authority — run someone else's copy and it spends THEIR OWN mandate or refuses. If no mandate exists for the actor, the step refuses and names the fix.

signet_target.description: Destination address (pay/transfer), the mint to trade into (swap), an address (portfolio) or the mint to price (price). For a WRITE it MUST be on the mandate's allowlist or the rail refuses. Templating: `{{input}}` is the run input and `{{upstream.<field>}}` reads the previous step's output. Not needed for 'metrics' or 'mandates'.

signet_value.description: Amount in BASE units — lamports for SOL, the mint's base units for an SPL token. Never a decimal. Templating: `{{input}}` is the run input, and `{{upstream.<field>}}` reads the PREVIOUS step's output — which is how a decided position size actually reaches the trade (`{{upstream.size_lamports}}`). Hard-coding an amount in a rig whose earlier step computes one is a bug: the strategy's sizing is then calculated and discarded. If the reference does not resolve, the field is EMPTY and the step refuses — a trade sized by a leftover constant is a trade nobody decided. Not needed for a read action.

skill.description: Registry skill name to bind this step to (discover via registry_search)

state.description: DECISION step only: what to decide about — a template reading {{input}} and {{upstream.<field>}}; empty = the upstream output.

sub_rig.description: Make this node a SUB-RIG step — the referenced SAVED rig runs here as a bounded sub-run (one level deep; runner-pays, shared budget, traces nested under this node). Pass {rig_id, name?} or a bare rig-id string (rig_search finds ids). Mutually exclusive with `skill`. ⚠ the canvas renders it as a labeled ⬡ block; its INNER edits go through you.

tool.description: Tool name to invoke on the endpoint (optional)

url.description: Plain-HTTP fetch target — the run performs a REAL HTTP request here via the SSRF-guarded proxy (optional; use with method + params + headers + secret_refs). `{{input}}` substitutes into the PATH or QUERY too (e.g. 'https://api.example.com/tokens/{{input}}'); the host stays fixed.

outputs.description: What the rig DECLARES IT PRODUCES — the contract's output side, shown on the canvas Output box and the product page. Same shapes as `input` (required is input-only). e.g. [{"label": "the audit report", "kind": "markdown"}].

state.description: SHARED STATE CHANNELS (stateful_graph) — named channels loop iterations read/write via `{{node.port}}` refs; `reducer` merges concurrent fan-out writes: 'last_write' (default) | 'append' | 'add'. Each {id, kind?, reducer?}.

structure_type.description: 'linear' (a simple chain — what the guided Builder produces), 'dag' (default; acyclic, parallel branches + real fan-in) or 'stateful_graph' (cyclic loops + conditional edge guards — the runtime evaluates guards and skips unfired branches for real; the Builder CANVAS can't edit it yet, so tell the owner edits go through you)

summary.description: Short human description of the flow (shows as the rig's name)

wallet_address.description: Wallet address that owns the rig (the scope the run reads)
